subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: What product/API shape should OpenClaw use for safe multi-index memory failover: a new multi-index memorySearch config, a memory-plugin-owned design, or a smaller fallback-recovery-only path?
rationale: Current policy treats config, provider fallback, persisted SQLite state, and memory plugin boundaries as compatibility-sensitive, and the request cannot be implemented safely without choosing the supported API and migration boundary first.

options.title: Design multi-index memorySearch
options.body: Approve a first-class per-model index design with explicit config, doctor migration, status output, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep scalar memorySearch
options.body: Decline multi-index support for now and handle only narrow fallback recovery or FTS degradation bugs in separate issues.

options.title: Move to memory plugin API design
options.body: Require the capability to be expressed through a memory plugin or SDK extension before changing core config.

recommendation.title: Design multi-index memorySearch
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class per-model index design with explicit config, doctor migration, status output, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to osolmaz, which is the strongest live ownership signal for choosing the product/API direction.
